clue.text: Girl said to be ill, but very chirpy

indicators.note: said signals that the word for being unwell is spoken, giving letters that only sound like it

parts.note: to be ill is to be sick
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl who is supposedly unwell nonetheless seems remarkably cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken as 'sick Ada', the phrase sounds like the insect; the cheerful-patient picture hides that 'chirpy' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The cicada is an insect famous for its loud, incessant chirping song, so it is about as chirpy as a creature gets.

clue.text: What it takes to argue different with an officer

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer

indicators.note: different signals that the word's letters are made unlike their original order

explanation.surface: Disputing a decision with a superior officer requires nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a quarrel with a superior; 'with' simply joins the two pieces, and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage is the bravery a hard act demands, as in the idiom about having what it takes.

clue.text: Sponge around with Cutler

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for around
Adge Cutler was the singer who founded the Wurzels, a West Country band

explanation.surface: A scrounger hangs about with a knife-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Adge Cutler led the Wurzels, a British folk-comedy band from Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to cadge, scrounging food or money from others without paying.

clue.text: Girl to notice up German river

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ad is a notice
the Mosel flows through western Germany

explanation.surface: A young woman goes to see a notice beside a river in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AD into DA; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Damosel is an archaic, poetic form of damsel, meaning a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Mother, then grandmother some time in the future

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
nana is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: First mum, then granny, will turn up eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: Mañana is Spanish for tomorrow, used in English for an unspecified later time, procrastination's watchword.

clue.text: £1000 taken from vicarage? That could be a sin

indicators.note: that could be suggests the remaining letters may form something else when reordered

parts.note: G stands for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds stolen from the vicar's house: surely wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove G from VICARAGE and rearrange the remaining letters ('That could be'); 'taken from' tells us which letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice, or greed, is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Philosopher is later to change his name

indicators.note: changing a name alters its letters, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thinker is going to adopt a new name in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change his name' rearranges ISLATERTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Plato.

clue.text: Off the boat? About time, darling

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: ashore means off a boat and onto land

explanation.surface: Landing from the ship, someone greets a beloved, saying it is about time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps ASHORE around T.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthore is an Irish term of endearment, meaning darling or treasure.

clue.text: Stirs up rage in French city

definitions.meaning: a city on the Maine in western France

explanation.surface: Something provokes fury in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb meaning provokes fury and the city in the Loire valley share one spelling.

clue.text: Light-hearted lady isn't last to be trashed by bigots

parts.note: something light-hearted is fun
a dame is a lady

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the letters of these words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Narrow-minded people want to ruin a cheerful woman who is not in last place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be trashed' scrambles the letters ISNTLAST; 'by' is a link joining wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamentalists hold rigidly to strict doctrine, and are often seen as intolerant of other views, much like bigots.

clue.text: Cutting these could get you into a scrape

definitions.text: Cutting these could get you into a scrape

parts.words: Cutting these could get you into a scrape
parts.note: to frolic about, which can land you in trouble; the letters of the frolics also rearrange into the word scrape

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is 'cut capers', to leap about friskily. 'Cutting' them can also mean rearranging their letters, which spells SCRAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Capers are playful leaps, and cutting capers means behaving in a lively, mischievous way that can lead to trouble.

clue.text: Turning out to get into vice

indicators.note: get is read as become or turn into, so these letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone is going bad and starting to take up wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' asks for the letters of INTO VICE to be rearranged; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An eviction is the act of turning tenants out of a property, the noun form of that expulsion.

clue.text: Labourer with an old bicycle

definitions.meaning: the Greek hero famous for performing twelve labours
a long-established British bicycle brand of the same name

explanation.surface: A workman rides a vintage bike.
explanation.walkthrough: Hercules was a British bicycle maker, popular in the mid-twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical strongman had to complete twelve labours, and the name was also borne by a classic British bike.

clue.text: Claim to put pounds above euro in petty cash

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: change is small coins, petty cash

indicators.note: above in a down clue puts the first piece on top, so earlier

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone demands that sterling be placed ahead of the euro in the office cash box.
explanation.walkthrough: Petty cash suggests an office tin, but here it is loose coins; 'above' sets the pounds before the euro in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A challenge can be a claim of right, as in a challenge demanding something be justified.

clue.text: There's trouble in a book

indicators.note: trouble means disturb, so these letters are stirred into another order

explanation.surface: Something in a book is causing difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges THERES; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a book of the Old Testament, named after the Jewish queen of Persia.

clue.text: Lights unknown in Ireland

parts.note: lights are animal lungs, a kind of offal
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Lamps of mysterious origin are seen somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lights' looks like lamps but means lungs sold as butcher's meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Offaly is a county in the Irish midlands, so it is a place found in Ireland.

clue.text: Transport required if going over land

indicators.note: going over in a down clue means turning the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: taken as written
acres are land

explanation.surface: Vehicles will be needed should one cross the territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns IF into FI; 'required' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiacre is a small horse-drawn hackney carriage, a form of transport for hire.

clue.text: R is the last of December

definitions.text: R is the last of December

parts.words: R is the last of December
parts.note: the letter R closes the word for a twelve-month period, and the closing of that period falls on the last day of December

explanation.walkthrough: R is the end of YEAR, so it is literally the year end; the year end also falls on the last day of December.
explanation.definitionFit: The year-end is the close of the calendar year, which falls on the last day of December.

clue.text: Crumpet may be, so to speak, in bed

definitions.text: Crumpet may be, so to speak, in bed

parts.words: Crumpet may be, so to speak, in bed
parts.note: a crumpet, the toasted griddle cake, is spread with butter; crumpet is also British slang for an attractive woman, and the second sense hints at a bedroom romp

explanation.walkthrough: A crumpet is a British teacake eaten toasted with butter; it is also slang for a desirable woman, which gives the saucy reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A toasted crumpet is spread with butter, so the teacake is typically served this way.

clue.text: Actor drawing on toilet walls

indicators.note: on here places the drawing upon the toilet, so the art follows the lavatory in the name

parts.note: bog is British slang for toilet
drawing is a form of art

explanation.surface: A performer is caught doodling graffiti in a lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on ... walls' sets the scene of graffiti on lavatory walls; BOG is British slang for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart was a celebrated Hollywood film actor.

clue.text: Do they help one to become competent in races?

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: TTs are the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races
able means competent

explanation.surface: Is someone asking whether certain pills give a runner an edge?
explanation.walkthrough: The TT races are motorcycle races held on the Isle of Man; 'to become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tablets are pills taken to help a patient recover, so they help one.

clue.text: Over 10, perhaps 11

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: ten is the number 10 in words

explanation.surface: A count goes beyond ten, maybe up to eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges OVER TEN; the answer is a football team, an eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is an English football club, and a football team is an eleven.

clue.text: Lord of Appeal?

parts.note: a peer whose name is attached to a charitable appeal, the poppy fund for ex-servicemen, rather than a Law Lord

explanation.walkthrough: A Lord of Appeal is a senior judge, but here it is the British field marshal whose name was given to the Haig Fund poppy appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Field Marshal Douglas Haig became an earl, and the poppy appeal for veterans was long known as the Haig Fund.

clue.text: Kick it? That's the last thing I'll do!

definitions.text: Kick it? That's the last thing I'll do!

parts.words: Kick it? That's the last thing I'll do!
parts.note: kicking this container is the idiom for dying, which is indeed the last thing anyone does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Kick the bucket' means to die; the speaker's refusal doubles as literal truth.
explanation.definitionFit: The bucket is the pail in the idiom about death, the final act of anyone's life.

clue.text: TUC severely criticised

parts.note: the letters of the trade union body read upwards in a down clue spell a short word, and read as instructions they give the clue word

explanation.surface: The trade union congress has been savaged.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress. The answer read as wordplay says CUT going UP, which in a down grid gives TUC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut up is British informal for harshly criticised or deeply upset.

clue.text: Result of losing one's mobile in Africa once?

definitions.text: Result of losing one's mobile in Africa once?

parts.words: Result of losing one's mobile in Africa once?
parts.note: losing a phone from a particular UK network leaves you liberated from it; the phrase is also a former Boer republic in southern Africa

explanation.walkthrough: Orange was a UK mobile network; being rid of it leaves you 'Orange-free'. The Orange Free State was a nineteenth-century Boer republic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orange Free State was an independent Boer republic in southern Africa, later a province of South Africa.

clue.text: Moving, stayed on course

indicators.note: moving signals that the letters of the next word shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A ship in motion held to its planned route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges STAYED.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady describes holding an unwavering direction, as a helmsman keeps a ship on course.

clue.text: Under fire first to last, reportedly showing style

indicators.note: first to last tells us to take the opening part of the word and shift it to the end
reportedly signals that the word for style is taken by its sound and spelt to match

parts.note: panache is flair or style

explanation.surface: Someone shows flair while being shot at.
explanation.walkthrough: PANACHE sounds like PAN-ASH ('reportedly'); 'first to last' moves the PAN to the end, giving ASH-PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ash-pan is the tray set beneath a grate to catch the falling ash, so it sits under the fire.
